signature.title: Signature Moment
signature.lead: A true story from one of Indonesia's toughest oversight missions.
signature.body: When OSS 2.0 was being built, 15.4 million+ existing business identification numbers could not stop for a single second. Our team stood as the independent guardian: layered methodology oversight, service continuity through transition and cutover, and validation of the KBLI 2020 → 2025 migration.
highlights: Oversight of 5 core OSS modules: Basic Requirements, Business Licensing & PB UMKU, Information Services, System Management
Service continuity — the existing OSS stayed stable without disruption during cutover
Validation of the KBLI 2020 → 2025 update and migration of 15.4M+ historical business IDs

play.title: Play Character
play.lead: Step into the block world: walk, run, jump, then build your own digital infrastructure.
play.hint: Every block is one of our real services. Your build is saved automatically in this browser. Raise the Meaningful Stack: Foundation → Craft → Quality → Change → Care.
play.ctaNote: You play as the Eric character in an isometric block arena. What you must build: the Meaningful Stack — five layers in order from ground to sky, I Foundation → II Craft → III Quality → IV Change → V Care. A block only stands on what is already solid, and pulling the foundation collapses what rests on it. Break and stack blocks to complete it — everything is saved in this browser, so your build is still there when you come back.

Denys Almaral. "Male Running (20 frames loop)" — Sketchfab, Free Standard license. The 20-frame loop (0.667 s @30fps) was sampled via the Viewer API; its knee & elbow flexion shapes are the run reference (runLoop.ts)
Perry J, Burnfield JM. Gait Analysis: Normal and Pathological Function, 2nd ed. Slack, 2010 — 60/40 stance/swing, ~60° swing knee flexion
Novacheck TF. The biomechanics of running. Gait & Posture 7(1):77–95, 1998 — 40% stance, ~100–120° swing knee flexion, trunk lean
Weyand PG, Sternlight DB, Bellizzi MJ, Wright S. J Appl Physiol 89(5):1991–1999, 2000 — step frequency plateaus → 1.9 cycles/s ceiling (~228 steps/min)
Cavanagh PR, Kram R. Med Sci Sports Exerc 21(4):467–479, 1989 — stride length grows with speed
Van Hooren B, et al. The Relationship Between Running Biomechanics and Running Economy. Sports Med 54(5), 2024 — short contact & efficient knee swing mark economical running
Physio-pedia: Running Biomechanics — the double float phase (both feet airborne) separates running from walking
The Movement System: Biomechanics of Running — elbows ~90° driven backwards, cadence 155–160 steps/min

Freelap USA: A Call to Arms — Sprint Mechanics Revisited. The elbow is not locked at 90°: it closes front-side and opens as the shoulder extends; hands travel hip-pocket → chin; shoulders and hands stay relaxed
De Vlieger D, et al. Speed-dependent changes in the arm swing during walking. PMC, 2025 — healthy-side shoulder sagittal ROM ~25–30°, growing with speed; mean elbow flexion ~41°

Rubio JE, et al. Differences in running biomechanics between young, healthy men and women carrying external loads. PMC, 2023 — men's trunk flexion is 16.9–24.6% greater than women's; Eric's ~15° run lean follows this masculine trait

Scharl T, et al. Gender Differences in the Dynamics and Kinematics of Running. Bioengineering 11(12):1261, 2024 — female runners show larger hip/pelvis ROM; Eric's masculine carriage: elbows hugged to the ribcage, sagittal arm swing, minimal lateral sway
cadence = v / stride; stride = 1.5 + (3.0 − 1.5)·speedNorm (metres per cycle)
knee flexion = lerp(1.05; 2.09 rad) ≈ 60° walk → 120° run; run curve SHAPE from the 20-key reference loop (periodic Catmull-Rom), amplitudes stay Eric's

arms counter-swing the legs: shoulder ±15° walk → ±35° run (hand hip-pocket → chin); elbow ~90° ± 21° at run with a sagittal hinge carried by the shoulder's posed rotation; abduction tightens +0.07 rad with speed (elbows hug the ribcage); palm pronates toward the thigh, fingers relaxed-curl

Owen NJ, Watkins J, Kilduff LP, Bevan HR, Bennett MA. Understanding the key phases of the countermovement jump force-time curve. Strength Cond J 40(4):96–106, 2018 — six phases: weighing, unweighting, braking, propulsion, flight, landing

Bobbert MF, Gerritsen KGM, Litjens MCA, Van Soest AJ. Why is countermovement jump height greater than squat jump height? Med Sci Sports Exerc 28(11):1402–1412, 1996 — countermovement adds push-off work
Komi PV, Bosco C. Utilization of stored elastic energy in leg extensor muscles by men and women. Med Sci Sports Exerc 10(4):261–265, 1978 — elastic energy during braking
Harman EA, Rosenstein MT, Frykman PN, Rosenstein RM. The effects of arms and countermovement on vertical jumping. Med Sci Sports Exerc 22(6):817–823, 1990 — arm swing adds ~10–11 cm
Lees A, Vanrenterghem J, De Clercq D. Understanding how an arm swing enhances performance in the vertical jump. J Biomech 37(12):1929–1940, 2004 — arm swing adds 8.6 cm
McHugh MP et al. Effect of countermovement depth on the neuromechanics of countermovement jumps. 2024 — dip depth & braking knee flexion
Petushek EJ. 2D video vs electrogoniometry: countermovement jump and landing knee flexion angle. Thesis, Northern Michigan University, 2011 — landing knee absorption
Linthorne NP. Analysis of standing vertical jumps using a force platform. Am J Phys 69(11):1198–1206, 2001 — flight-time & impulse–momentum methods
h = v₀² / 2g · t_flight = 2v₀ / g (v₀ 7.6 · g 24 → h ≈ 1.20 units · t ≈ 0.63 s)
h = g·t² / 8 (flight-time method, Linthorne 2001)
J = ∫F dt = m·Δv (impulse–momentum: take-off & landing absorption)
Semi-implicit Euler projectile: v += −g·dt; y += v·dt
Frame-rate independent exponential damp: x += (target − x)·(1 − e^(−λ·dt))
desired = clamp(diff·4, ±MAX_SPEED); dv capped by ACCELERATION·dt
phase += cadence·2π·dt — feet locked to the ground, no foot-sliding
cell = floor(hitPoint ± normal·0.5) — block placement via face normal

lines: Welcome to Jakarta 2045! The sky is busy, but it keeps its order.
Hello! I have kept this stage since 2041. Lovely to be greeted.
Look up: that is the second-class air lane. Please do not jaywalk.
Monas burns light all night now. The pride of us all.
Coffee? I do not drink. But there is a good shop at stage three.
PT Cartenz built my network. I was made to greet, not to replace.
If you are lost, follow the ribbon of light on the ground. It always leads to the horizon.
Your greeting is logged. Thank you for stopping by, human.
